newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says Eurofighter necessary-German paper.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Eurofighter necessary-German paper.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel believes the four-nation Eurofighter is necessary both in terms of German national and a wider European interest, a German newspaper quoted him as saying on Thursday.

"I want the Eurofighter and consider it necessary both in the national and European interest. Now it's a question of agreeing an acceptable financial model with the manufacturer DASA," he was quoted as saying by the newspaper Die Welt in an advance summary of an article to appear on Friday.
The jet is being jointly developed by Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, British Aerospace, Spain's CASA and Italy's Alenia.

"I have always fought for Eurofighter," Waigel was further quoted as saying, referring to lengthy debate as to whether Germany and Europe needed the military aircraft, which is expected to cost Germany alone a total of 23 billion marks ($13.4 billion).
German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said last week that Waigel had pledged that funds to allow German participation in Eurofighter would be approved following cabinet budget meetings next month.

Ruehe told the Bild newspaper he would seek the approval of German parliament for the venture if assured of a "full budget and the additional means" that are expected to result from a redirection of state aid previously provided to DASA.
